IBM

Enterprise technology spanning AI, hybrid cloud, infrastructure, security, and software – one of Arrow ECS UK's broadest and deepest vendor relationships.

Data Centre Business Intelligence Cloud Security Networking IoT and Edge DevOps

Overview

IBM is one of the world's oldest and most diversified technology companies, with a portfolio that spans every layer of enterprise IT. Through Arrow ECS UK, IBM's portfolio covers infrastructure hardware (Power Systems, IBM Z mainframes, storage), a deep software catalogue (Db2, MQ, CICS, WebSphere, OpenPages), an expanding AI platform (watsonx), and a security suite (QRadar SIEM, Guardium data security, Verify IAM). IBM also delivers cloud services – IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS – available via ArrowSphere.

For sales teams, IBM is a high-value, long-cycle vendor. Deals are often infrastructure-led (a Power or Storage refresh) but the real expansion opportunity is in software and AI layered on top of that infrastructure – and in the adjacent vendors that complement IBM's platform.

Arrow-Carried Portfolio

IBM Power Systems
RISC-based enterprise servers running AIX, IBM i, and Linux. Dominant in banking, insurance, and ERP workloads. Power10 generation delivers on-chip AI inference.
Data Centre AIX / IBM i ERP
IBM Z / LinuxONE
Mainframe platform for mission-critical transaction processing. LinuxONE is the open-source variant. Unmatched availability (99.99999%), security, and throughput at scale.
Data Centre Mainframe Security

FlashSystem all-flash arrays for primary storage; IBM Tape (TS series) for long-term archival and ransomware-resilient air-gapped backup. Also includes IBM Storwize and SAN Volume Controller.
Data Centre All-Flash Tape / Archive

watsonx.ai for building and deploying foundation models; watsonx.data for governed data lakehouse; watsonx.governance for AI lifecycle compliance. IBM's primary AI growth vehicle.

Cross-sell & Expansion Opportunities

Splunk
SIEM Alongside or Instead of QRadar
Where a customer already runs Splunk, IBM QRadar can feed into it as a data source. Where QRadar is the SIEM, Splunk may already be in use for operational analytics – the two coexist more often than you'd expect in large enterprises. Leads with QRadar should be aware Splunk will be on the shortlist.
Commvault
Enterprise Data Protection on IBM Infrastructure
Commvault has strong IBM integrations including IBM Spectrum Protect (now Storage Protect) awareness and IBM Tape support. In large enterprises with mixed IBM and non-IBM environments, Commvault can act as a single backup platform across all of it.
NetApp
Storage Complement for Non-IBM Workloads
Customers with IBM storage for IBM workloads (Power/Z) frequently use NetApp for their VMware and file workloads. IBM and NetApp coexist naturally in the same data centre. A storage conversation touching one often surfaces the other.
SNYK
DevSecOps Alongside IBM DevOps Tools
Customers buying IBM UrbanCode or IBM Engineering tools are building DevOps practices. SNYK plugs into those pipelines to add developer-first security scanning for code, containers, and open-source dependencies – a natural expansion sell in any IBM DevOps conversation.
Entrust
HSM for IBM Z Cryptographic Security
IBM Z's built-in CPACF and Crypto Express processors often operate alongside external HSM infrastructure for key escrow and high-assurance certificate management. Entrust nShield HSMs provide the FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware root of trust that regulated customers require alongside IBM Z – a natural expansion in any IBM Z security conversation.
HCLSoftware
IBM Middleware Heritage – Legacy Modernisation
HCLSoftware acquired several IBM software products (Domino, Connections, BigFix, Unica). Customers running these alongside remaining IBM middleware are a natural combined conversation. HCL and IBM frequently appear together in the same enterprise accounts.
Turbonomic / IBM Automation
FinOps & Resource Optimisation
IBM Turbonomic (now part of IBM) is often sold separately into cloud and virtualisation conversations. Customers with IBM Cloud spend or hybrid VMware/IBM environments can reduce waste significantly – a strong conversation when procurement is pressuring on cloud bills.
OPSWAT
OPSWAT Events into IBM QRadar for SIEM Enrichment
OPSWAT MetaDefender generates detailed file scan, CDR, and device compliance events. IBM QRadar can ingest these events via syslog or API, correlating file-based threats with broader network and identity activity in the SOC. In environments running IBM QRadar where OT, air-gapped networks, or removable media control is also required, OPSWAT is a complementary data source and control layer that strengthens the overall security posture.
F5 Networks
F5 WAF & APM Events into IBM QRadar
F5 BIG-IP WAF and Access Policy Manager generate detailed application-layer security events. IBM QRadar can ingest F5 syslog feeds, adding application security visibility to the SOC alongside network and identity event data. F5 BIG-IP hardware is also deployed on IBM infrastructure in enterprise data centres – IBM Power and IBM Z environments commonly co-exist with F5 ADC layers in front of their application interfaces.
Black Duck
Open-Source Security in the IBM DevOps Pipeline
Customers building software with IBM DevOps tools (IBM UrbanCode Deploy, IBM Engineering Lifecycle Management) are running CI/CD pipelines where Black Duck provides open-source security scanning. IBM UK itself appears as a Black Duck end user in Arrow's 2025 channel data – confirming co-deployment at enterprise scale. Any IBM DevOps conversation with a customer that builds software internally should include a discussion of their open-source security posture.

Competitive Landscape

Vendors you are likely to encounter in the same deals. Knowing the landscape helps frame IBM's strengths.

Dell Technologies
Infrastructure / Storage
Dell PowerEdge competes with IBM Power in x86 workloads; Dell PowerStore/Unity competes with IBM FlashSystem in mid-range all-flash. Dell is the most common alternative in storage deals. IBM's advantage: Power and Z workloads have no credible Dell equivalent – they're platform decisions, not commodity comparisons.
HPE
Infrastructure / Storage
HPE Alletra and Nimble compete with IBM FlashSystem; HPE ProLiant with IBM Power on Linux workloads. HPE GreenLake (as-a-service) is a counterpart to IBM's hybrid cloud model. IBM differentiates on workload affinity – particularly for IBM i, AIX, and mainframe-adjacent workloads where HPE has no presence.
Palo Alto Networks
Security (SIEM / SOAR)
Palo Alto Cortex XSIAM is the primary modern alternative to IBM QRadar in SIEM/SOAR consolidation deals. Palo Alto leads on UX and AI-native narrative; IBM leads on depth of integration with mainframe and IBM middleware audit data, and on regulated-industry compliance posture.
Microsoft Azure
Cloud / AI
Azure competes with IBM Cloud for cloud workloads, and Microsoft Copilot competes with IBM watsonx in enterprise AI. IBM's differentiation is governance, data privacy, and suitability for regulated industries – watsonx.governance has no direct Microsoft equivalent. IBM also wins where customers need on-premises AI inference (Power10 on-chip).
Pure Storage
All-Flash Storage
Pure FlashArray is a common alternative to IBM FlashSystem in pure all-flash deals. Pure's Evergreen model (no forklift upgrades) is a strong commercial differentiator. IBM counters with deeper integration with IBM workloads, Safeguarded Copy (immutable snapshots), and the full-stack story with IBM Spectrum Virtualize.

Ideal Customer Profile

Organisation Size
Enterprise and upper mid-market. IBM hardware especially targets organisations with 500+ employees. IBM software licensing scales across all sizes.
Verticals
Financial services, insurance, retail banking, public sector, healthcare, telco, and utilities – particularly those running legacy IBM platforms (COBOL, IBM i, mainframe).
Trigger Events
End-of-support on older Power / Storage hardware; mainframe capacity upgrade; AI strategy mandate; SOC modernisation; data governance / compliance project.
Key Personas
CTO, IT Director, Head of Infrastructure, CISO (for QRadar/Guardium), Chief Data Officer (for watsonx). IBM decisions rarely happen below Director level.
